locator: I.42 [21–24], scriptural confession and doctrinal applications
interpretation: One coherent reading of the same proper-divine-being unity confession, not independent new historical claims. [21] adduces Scripture; [22] distinguishes the highest divine cause from dependent everlasting/wise beings or others called gods; [23] identifies two independent first principles, neither causing the other, as the central opposing case; [24] applies the confession against several-gods language about Father and Son. Exact reuse is at-most-one proper divine Being, not at-most-one necessarily existing individual, no dependent beings named gods, or one divine person. The doctrinal references explain source scope and are not independent historical/theological verification or an argument defeating plural roots. No source/scriptural truth, formal proof, ordinary Ontic dictionary or divine-person identity is asserted.
